evidence.item: L1 top-of-book feasibility fixture (NoPartialFillExchange and PartialFillExchange)

A_marketable_ioc_fill.setup: Static book (bid 10.00/100, ask 10.02/100); constant_order_latency(70ms,70ms); power_prob_queue_model(2.0). IOC buy limit submitted at ask+$0.01 collar. Run under both no_partial_fill_exchange and partial_fill_exchange.
A_marketable_ioc_fill.hand_expectation: FILLED at 10.02 under both exchange models (ack_new's price_tick>=best_ask_tick branch fires purely from L1 best-ask depth; the single L1 level's qty=100 fully covers the order's qty=10, so partial-fill semantics never trigger)
A_marketable_ioc_fill.actual_result: FILLED at 10.02, exec_qty=10.0, leaves_qty=0.0 under both no_partial_fill and partial_fill -- matches, identical

B_ioc_expiry.setup: Same book; order priced off ask=10.02 (limit 10.03) submitted at 50ms; ask re-quotes to 10.06 at 100ms, before the order's 70ms entry latency lands it at the exchange at 120ms. Run under both exchange models.
B_ioc_expiry.hand_expectation: EXPIRED under both (10.03 < prevailing ask 10.06 at arrival; IOC/FOK do not rest, per both nopartialfillexchange.rs and partialfillexchange.rs ack_new else-branches)
B_ioc_expiry.actual_result: EXPIRED, exec_qty=0.0, leaves_qty=10.0 under both no_partial_fill and partial_fill -- matches, identical

C_queue_trade_depletion_needs_side.setup: Resting GTC buy at bid=10.00 (qty 20 ahead); five TRADE_EVENT prints of qty 10 at 10.00, once with SELL_EVENT (aggressor hits the bid) and once with no side bit at all (our L1/SIP reality). Run under both exchange models.
C_queue_trade_depletion_needs_side.hand_expectation: with_side: FILLED under both (queue_model.trade() consumes queue ahead via EXCH_SELL_TRADE_EVENT, matching the resting Side::Buy order in both nopartialfillexchange.rs and partialfillexchange.rs). without_side: stays NEW under both (a bare TRADE_EVENT matches neither EXCH_BUY_TRADE_EVENT nor EXCH_SELL_TRADE_EVENT in either exchange model, so it is silently dropped and queue_model.trade() is never called).
C_queue_trade_depletion_needs_side.actual_result: with_side: FILLED, exec_qty=5.0 under both. without_side: NEW, exec_qty=0.0 under both -- matches, identical

evidence.l1_verdict_changes_with_partial_fill_exc: All three scenarios produced byte-identical order_status/exec_qty/leaves_qty results under no_partial_fill_exchange and partial_fill_exchange. This is expected for this specific fixture: every scenario's single L1 level has enough quantity (100) to fully satisfy the order (10 or 5), so PartialFillExchange's extra behavior (partial fills across a level when quantity is insufficient) never activates. A fixture with an order quantity exceeding the touch's quoted size would be needed to actually exercise the divergence between the two exchange models; that is a documented remaining gap, not claimed to be covered here.
source_citations: hftbacktest/src/backtest/proc/partialfillexchange.rs (same branches, present at similar line numbers)
docs/data.rst (qty==0 at a DEPTH_EVENT price removes that level)

evidence.rule: trade price >= ask -> buy aggressor; trade price <= bid -> sell aggressor; otherwise the tick test (compare to the previous trade price).
evidence.setup: Identical resting order and trade-print setup to Scenario C, except the side bit fed to hftbacktest is not hard-coded: each trade prints at 10.00 with bid=10.00/ask=10.02, so trade_px <= bid classifies every print as a sell aggressor under Lee-Ready before the SELL_EVENT bit is applied.
evidence.result: All 5 trades classified 'sell'; resulting order_status FILLED, exec_qty 5.0 -- matches Scenario C's with_side=True result exactly, restoring trade-driven queue depletion from L1/SIP-shaped data via a data-preparation step external to hftbacktest.
evidence.claim_boundary: This is OUR proposed data-preparation step, explicitly presented as such -- Lee-Ready is a classic market-microstructure heuristic (Lee & Ready 1991), not an hftbacktest feature, and it is an imperfect proxy for the true (unobserved) aggressor side, not a substitute for real exchange-reported side data.

feasible_for: Order acceptance/rejection logic driven by top-of-book crossing (marketable IOC/limit fills, GTX/limit rejection at the touch)
IOC/FOK immediate-fill-or-expire semantics, decided purely from best-bid/best-ask depth
Constant and per-symbol latency modelling (entry + response), independent of depth granularity
FlatPerTradeFeeModel / TradingValueFeeModel cost accounting on realized fills

Both no_partial_fill_exchange and partial_fill_exchange for the crossing/expiry paths above -- verified identical on this fixture (see l1_verdict_changes_with_partial_fill_exchange=false, with the noted caveat about order size vs. touch size)
not_feasible_or_meaningless_for: Probabilistic queue-position models (RiskAdverse/Power/Log) that key off trade-print volume at the touch: hftbacktest's exchange models only apply a trade to queue depletion when the event carries a BUY_EVENT/SELL_EVENT aggressor bit (EXCH_BUY_TRADE_EVENT/EXCH_SELL_TRADE_EVENT), in both no_partial_fill_exchange and partial_fill_exchange. Alpaca's consolidated SIP tape has no aggressor side, so these models silently receive zero trade-driven queue depletion under raw L1 data -- demonstrated empirically in Scenario C under both exchange models, not just asserted.
The L3 FIFO queue model, which needs individual order add/cancel/execute events (order_id-level), categorically unavailable from L1 or even standard L2 SIP quotes.
Any depth-percentile / multi-level queue heuristic that reads levels beyond the touch (our L1 feed only ever has one level per side).
l1_feasibility_verdict.mitigation: A Lee-Ready (or similar) aggressor-side inference step, applied as data preparation before feeding hftbacktest, restores trade-driven queue depletion in this fixture (see the Lee-Ready evidence item). This makes the probabilistic queue models usable on SIP-derived data at the cost of introducing inference error the true exchange-reported side would not have; that error is not quantified here.
l1_feasibility_verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading hftbacktest/src/backtest/proc/{nopartialfillexchange,partialfillexchange}.rs (both exchange models) and reproducing all code paths (depth-crossing fill/expiry, trade-driven queue depletion, and Lee-Ready-restored depletion) with a hand-verified synthetic fixture; every L1-driven path matched hand computation exactly under both exchange models, and the side-dependent path was empirically shown to be a no-op without an aggressor bit -- and restored by the proposed inference step.
